questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The final performance of the play was
far more spectacular than the director
initially imagined during the rehearsals.
options_hi: The final performance of the play was
far more spectacular than the director
initially imagined during the rehearsals.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “imagined” with “had imagined”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Past Perfect for Prior Expectations

This follows the logic of the "Earlier Past." When you compare a past reality to what someone thought beforehand, you are dealing with two different points in the past:

  1. Action 1 (Earlier): The director forming an imagination or mental picture during rehearsals.

  2. Action 2 (Later): The actual final performance taking place.

Since the imagining happened before the performance, the verb "imagined" must be in the Past Perfect Tense (had + V3).

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...performance... was far more spectacular than the director initially imagined..."

  • Was: Simple Past ($V_2$). This is the baseline for the "now" of the story.

  • Imagined: This action was completed during the rehearsals, which happened before the performance.



Corrected Sentence

The final performance of the play was far more spectacular than the director had initially imagined during the rehearsals.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: The exam was easier than I had thought it would be.

Example 2 ✅: The hotel was much smaller than it had appeared in the brochures.

Example 3 ✅: She found that the city had changed more than she had anticipated.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  • Initial/Previously: Words like initially, previously, earlier, or beforehand often hint that the action belongs further back in time, requiring the Past Perfect.

  • The Comparison Clue: In comparisons using "than," if the first part is $V_2$ (was, felt, looked), the second part is a prime candidate for had + V3.

  • Consistency: Always check if the "thinking" (expecting, assuming, imagining) happened before the "seeing/doing." If yes, add the had.

questions.q_en:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

People believe that the company manipulated its financial statements.
questions.q_hi:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

People believe that the company manipulated its financial statements.
options_en: It is believed that the company manipulated its financial statements.
The company is believed to have manipulated its financial statements.
Both A and B
The company was believed that it manipulated its financial statements.
options_hi: It is believed that the company manipulated its financial statements.
The company is believed to have manipulated its financial statements.
Both A and B
The company was believed that it manipulated its financial statements.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C)

With either “It is believed that the company manipulated its financial statements” or “The company is believed to have manipulated its financial statements.”

📌 Rule / Concept: Reporting Verb – Dual Passive Structure (That-Clause & Infinitive Form)

When the active structure is: Subject (People/They) + reporting verb (believe, say, think, expect, consider, report, etc.) + that-clause, it can be converted into passive in two correct ways:

1️⃣ It + be + V³ + that-clause
2️⃣ Object of the clause + be + V³ + to-infinitive

If the verb inside the “that-clause” is in past tense, it usually converts into perfect infinitive (to have + V³).

Structure: People believe that X did something.
→ It is believed that X did something.
→ X is believed to have done something.

In Question - Main verb = believe
That-clause verb = manipulated (simple past)

So, two valid passive forms are:

✔ It is believed that the company manipulated its financial statements.
✔ The company is believed to have manipulated its financial statements.

Since both structures are grammatically correct and acceptable in formal English, the correct answer is Option (C) Both A and B.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Reporting verbs allow two passive forms. If the verb inside the clause is in past tense, use “to have + V³.” Avoid mixing clause and infinitive structures. Banking and SSC Mains frequently test whether you know both valid passive patterns.

questions.q_en: You believe that the revised policy will stabilize the market sentiment, ______?
questions.q_hi: You believe that the revised policy will stabilize the market sentiment, ______?
options_en: will it
don’t you
won’t it
doesn’t it
options_hi: will it
don’t you
won’t it
doesn’t it
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) - “don’t you”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Matrix Clause Rule (Main Clause Determines the Tag)

In complex sentences containing subordinate clauses, the question tag is based on the main (matrix) clause, not the embedded clause.

Examiners often trap students by making them focus on the subordinate clause.

💢 Application to the Given Question

Main clause: You believe

Subordinate clause: that the revised policy will stabilize the market sentiment

The subject of the sentence is you, not “the revised policy”.

The main verb is believe (simple present).

So we use do-support: believe → don’t you?

The tag must agree with the main clause subject and verb, not the embedded statement.

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅- You think he is guilty, don’t you?

Example 2 ✅ - You suppose they will resign, don’t you?

Example 3 ✅ - You expect the results to improve, don’t you?

🧠 Things to Remember

  • Always identify the main clause first.

  • Ignore subordinate “that” clauses while forming the tag.

  • Tag must match subject + auxiliary of the matrix clause.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

Violence suddenly __________ in the city after the controversial announcement.
questions.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

Violence suddenly __________ in the city after the controversial announcement.
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (3).

English Explanation: “Break out” means to begin suddenly, especially in reference to events like war, violence, fire, disease, or chaos. In the sentence, violence suddenly began in the city after the controversial announcement. Therefore, “broke out” correctly conveys the idea of something starting abruptly and unexpectedly. “Break up” means to separate or disperse. “Break down” means to stop functioning or to collapse emotionally. “Break into” means to enter forcibly or suddenly start doing something (like laughing). Since the context refers to violence starting suddenly, “broke out” is the most appropriate fit.

1. Broke up (अलग होना / बिखर जाना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी समूह का बिखर जाना या संबंध का समाप्त होना।
Example: The crowd broke up after the speech ended. (भाषण खत्म होने के बाद भीड़ बिखर गई।)

2. Broke down (खराब होना / भावनात्मक रूप से टूट जाना)
Meaning in Hindi: मशीन का खराब हो जाना या व्यक्ति का भावनात्मक रूप से टूट जाना।
Example: His car broke down on the way to the office. (उसकी गाड़ी दफ्तर जाते समय खराब हो गई।)

3. Broke out (अचानक शुरू होना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी घटना का अचानक शुरू हो जाना।
Example 1: A fire broke out in the examination hall due to a short circuit. (शॉर्ट सर्किट के कारण परीक्षा कक्ष में आग लग गई।)
Example 2: An argument broke out between the two teams. (दोनों टीमों के बीच अचानक बहस शुरू हो गई।)

4. Broke into (ज़बरदस्ती घुसना / अचानक शुरू करना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी जगह में जबरन प्रवेश करना या अचानक कुछ करना।
Example: The thief broke into the house at night. (चोर रात में घर में घुस गया।)

that the cyclonic storm is gaining momentum as it
moved closer to the coastal regions of Odisha.

options_hi: The meteorologist explained to the press
that the cyclonic storm is gaining momentum as it
moved closer to the coastal regions of Odisha.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “is gaining” with “was gaining”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Sequence of Tenses (Indirect Speech)

If the Principal Verb is in the Past Tense (e.g., said, explained, told, announced), the verb in the Subordinate Clause must also be in a Past Tense.

💢 Application to the Given Question - The reporting verb "explained" is in the Simple Past. Therefore, the subsequent action describing the storm must align with that past timeframe. Using "is gaining" (Present Continuous) creates a tense mismatch, as it implies a present action linked to a past explanation. To maintain symmetry with both "explained" and the later verb "moved," it must be changed to "was gaining."

While interest rate adjustments can influence borrowing and investment, their effectiveness is frequently [----1----] by structural weaknesses such as low productivity and fiscal imbalance. Moreover, prolonged reliance on accommodative policies may [--2---] asset bubbles, distorting market signals and widening inequality. Investors, reacting to such volatility, often adopt a [----3----] stance, prioritizing short-term gains over long-term fundamentals. Policymakers therefore face the challenge of designing a [----4----] economic strategy that promotes sustainable growth while preserving financial stability.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [1] :

• Validated suggests confirmation, not limitation.
• Synchronized refers to coordination, irrelevant to reduced effectiveness.

📌 Rule / Concept: Relative Adverbs of Time – “It was... ago... when/that”

In formal English, when a sentence structure begins with "It was + [Time Duration] + ago", the word "ago" identifies a specific point in the past. To connect this point to the action that followed, we use a relative clause.

When: Acts as a relative adverb of time to link the event to the time mentioned.

That: Acts as a relative pronoun/conjunction to introduce the defining clause.

The "Since" Error: "Since" is used to show a duration from a past point to the present (e.g., It has been five days since...). It is logically inconsistent to pair "since" with "ago" because "ago" marks a completed past moment, while "since" marks a continuing duration.

❌ Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1 ❌: It was a month ago since we last spoke.

Wrong example 2 ❌: It was in 1990 ago that the company was founded. (Redundant use of 'ago' with a specific year).

✅ Corrected Sentence

It was more than fifty-five weeks ago when she last met me nearby the Taj hotel in Mumbai. (OR)

It was more than fifty-five weeks ago that she last met me nearby the Taj hotel in Mumbai.

📌 Rule / Concept: Full Inversion with "Here" and "There"

When a sentence begins with the adverbs "Here" or "There" to point out something or describe a dramatic action in the present, Full Inversion is used. This means the verb is placed before the noun subject.

Important Exception: If the subject is a Personal Pronoun (he, she, it, they, you), inversion does not take place (e.g., "Here he comes" is correct, NOT "Here comes he").

💢 Application to the Given Question

Here comes the chief guest of the evening...

In this sentence, the adverb "Here" starts the sentence. The subject is "the chief guest," which is a noun. Following the rule for nouns, the verb "comes" is correctly placed before the subject. Since the subject is singular, the singular verb "comes" is used, and the structure is perfectly inverted.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: There goes the bell for the final lap!

Example 2 ✅: Here are the keys you were looking for earlier.

Example 3 ✅: There stands the statue of the great leader.

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (D)- The blanks should be filled with the singularized fraction "One-third" and the plural verb "have."

Rule/Concept: Singular Fractions & Plural Noun Agreement

Fraction Rule: If the numerator (the first number) is one, the denominator must be singular (e.g., One-third, One-fourth). If the numerator is more than one, it becomes plural (Two-thirds).

Agreement Rule: For fractions, the verb agrees with the noun following "of". If the noun is plural, the verb must be plural.

Logic Breakdown:

The Fraction (Blank 1): Since the numerator is "One," the denominator must be singular: "One-third." This eliminates options (A) and (C).

The Noun: Look at the noun after "of"—it is "the specialized surgeons." "Surgeons" is a plural noun.

The Verb (Blank 2): Because the noun "surgeons" is plural, the verb must also be plural to match it. "Have" is the correct plural choice. This eliminates option (B).

The Distractor: The long phrase "working in the newly established neurosurgery department" is added to create distance between the subject and the verb, hoping you will lose track of the plural "surgeons."

Correct Sentence: One-third of the specialized surgeons... have decided to undergo further training.
